claims.summary: At (4,4), on the events of cor:comparable-gap-stacks, for N large: for nested lattice down-sets D_0 >= ... >= D_(K-1) (unions of W-cells, W = 2^(-l_1)) with extended 1-Lipschitz profiles phi_i, every boundary of grid length at least l_0 > 0, and g = m W y* sum 1_(D_i) of discrete cost at most 2, v = m y*: if the layers are partitioned into q classes such that consecutive members i < j of each class c have 2 gamma_c W <= phi_i - phi_j <= 2 lambda_c gamma_c W where the strip between them meets the square (gamma_c, lambda_c >= 1; lambda-bar the height-weighted mean of lambda_c, lambda+ = max lambda_c, gamma-bar = max gamma_c), then |D(g)| <= C sqrt(N log N)(1 + (1 + 1/l_0)(1 + lambda-bar (log(v/2))^(-1/4))) + C l_0^(-1) sqrt N ((log(4 lambda+ gamma-bar))^(3/4) + (log q)^(3/4))(log(v/2))^(-1/4), C universal; at the target when lambda-bar <= (log(v/2))^(1/4), log q <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(v/2))^(1/3), and lambda+ gamma-bar <= v or log(4 lambda+ gamma-bar) <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(v/2))^(1/3). Residue classes mod M: the bound with q = M when every M-step gap phi_i - phi_(i+M) is comparable; hierarchical gaps 2W 2^(nu(i)) with largest valuation up to c(log N)^(2/3)(log v)^(1/3) among them.
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections by one medium reviewer in two passes: linearity over the classes, each a one-height chain of cost at most 2 (its increments at most g's, psi_4^* nondecreasing) satisfying cor:comparable-gap-stacks' hypotheses; that corollary's proof in its form proportional to each class's height a_c, with v' = max(v, a); Jensen's inequality for the concave x (log_2(v'/x) + 1)^(3/4) over the q classes, and subadditivity of x^(3/4).
claims.rationale: Extends cor:comparable-gap-stacks from one class to q classes at the cost (log q)^(3/4), so stacks whose consecutive gap ratios are unbounded, periodic patterns and hierarchical gaps up to valuation c(log N)^(2/3)(log v)^(1/3) among them, are at the target; a larger subclass of the one-height chains cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) asks.
claims.next_action: The long hierarchies, largest valuation near (1/2) log_2 K, where both the block count and the residue count are about K^(1/2) and the residues' texture mesh costs (log N)^(3/4): by the adapted partition through lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b), or one ramp for the union of the classes with a single texture.
